profile.stagger_pattern: No stagger. All 7 seats (Mayor, 2 Councilors-at-Large, 4 Ward Councilors) are elected concurrently every 4 years at a nonpartisan election held the 2nd Tuesday in May; terms run July 1 to June 30. Cycles touching the 2019-2026 panel: 2016-05-10 (seats 2019 through 2020-06-30), 2020-05-12, 2024-05-14. 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2025 and 2026 are structural holdover years, not gaps.

run_log.detail: NJ registry entry read. Confirmed: NJ state election PDFs carry no municipal races; county clerk is the route. Montclair = Essex County, Council-Manager, nonpartisan May, all seats concurrent every 4 years. Registry correctly flags Montclair as Council-Manager but does NOT state its mayor-selection method; resolved independently (see profile step).

Montclair operates under the 1923 Municipal Manager form: 7 elected officials (Mayor, 2 Councilors-at-Large, 4 Ward Councilors), all elected together at a nonpartisan election on the 2nd Tuesday in May every 4 years, terms July 1 - June 30. Cycles: 2016-05-10, 2020-05-12, 2024-05-14. Every other panel year is a holdover. Term boundary of July 1 confirmed three ways: the 2024 inauguration was held Monday July 1 2024 (montclairlocal.news/2024/07/inauguration-of-montclairs-historic-new-council/); the Harrison appointment article states the winner of the Nov 2026 special election 'would serve until July 1, 2028'; the DCA Mayors Directory gives Baskerville term_start 2024-07-01.

BOTH panel cycles sourced from the Essex County Clerk's official results, via the Clarity JSON API rather than the robots-blocked Clarity web UI. Method: essexclerk.com/Election/ (fetches fine to curl with a browser UA; no robots.txt - the host 404s it) lists every election back to 2017 with its Clarity election id. Then GET https://results.enr.clarityelections.com/NJ/Essex/{id}/current_ver.txt -> version, then /{id}/{ver}/json/en/summary.json -> full contest/candidate/vote arrays as plain JSON. 2020 = id 103451 ver 246746 (listed as '2020 Special Municipal Elections' - the May 12 2020 election was converted to all-vote-by-mail by executive order, which is why the clerk labelled it 'Special'; there is no separate '2020 May Municipal' entry). 2024 = id 121184 ver 339247. Contest labels are 'Mayor-Montclair' / 'Montclair For Councilor At Large' (Vote For 2) / 'Montclair {N}st Ward For Councilor' in 2020, and 'For Mayor for Montclair' / 'For Councilmembers At-Large for Montclair' / 'For Member of the Council for Montclair {N}st Ward' in 2024. Verbatim totals - 2020: Mayor Sean M. Spiller 5445, Renee E. Baskerville MD 5250, write-in 53. At-Large (VF2): Peter Yacobellis 5472, Bob Russo 4915, Roger S. Terry 4577, James Cotter 4311, Carmel Loughman 1587, write-in 36. W1 William Hurlock 1681 / John Hearn 1241. W2 Robin Schlager 1763 / Christina 'Chrissy' Thomas 1305. W3 Lori Price Abrams 1295 / Maggie Joralemon 1001. W4 David Cummings 1915 unopposed. 2024: Mayor Renee E. Baskerville 3805, Chrissy Thomas 3494. At-Large (VF2): Susan Shin Andersen 4445, Carmel Loughman 4213, Robert J. Russo 3781. W1 Erik D'Amato 1242 / Shivaun Gaines 820. W2 Eileen Birmingham 1604 / Ilmar Vanderer 601. W3 Rahum Williams 624 / Roddy Moore 526 / Wendy A. Tiburcio 240. W4 Aminah Toler 658 / Zina Floyd 526 / Patricia A. Hurt 365.

2016-05-10 cycle NOT retrieved as a results record - the Essex County Clerk's results index only reaches back to 2017, so no Clarity id exists for it, and montclairlocal.news has no May-June 2016 results article in its WP index. The 2019 / first-half-2020 roster is therefore sourced from dated 2019 news coverage naming each officeholder rather than from the election record; those rows are marked medium confidence. NOT recorded as a cycle row (it falls outside the panel window). TRAP AVOIDED: a WebSearch offered patch.com/new-jersey/montclair/just-in-final-local-election-results as the 2016 results with 'Robert Russo 3,503 / Rich McMahon 2,731'; fetching the page shows it is datelined Wed, May 16, 2012 and reports the 2012 election. This is the brief's 'undated republished archive content' failure mode, arriving via a search summary. Those totals were discarded.

Four mid-term changes found, all via the montclairlocal.news WordPress REST API (wp-json/wp/v2/posts?search=&after=&before=&per_page=&_fields=date,link,title,content - the content field returns full verbatim article bodies, so no summarizer sits in the trust path). (1) 2019-06-25: council voted 3-2 to appoint at-large councilor Rich McMahon Deputy Mayor over 4th Ward councilor Renee Baskerville, breaking the ward rotation the 2016 slate had agreed; yes Spiller/Hurlock/McMahon, no Baskerville/Schlager, abstain Russo/Jackson. (2) 2023-10-12: Councilor-at-Large Peter Yacobellis announced his resignation (Thursday, Oct 12 2023 - weekday checks out). (3) 2023-10-18: council voted 4-2 (yes Spiller, Hurlock, Schlager, Price Abrams; no Cummings, Russo) to appoint Roger Terry, Montclair NAACP president and a former at-large councilor 2008-2012, to the vacancy - Wednesday Oct 18 2023, weekday checks out. Seat vacant 2023-10-12 to 2023-10-18. (4) 2025-09-12: Councilor-at-Large Carmel Loughman resigned just over a year into a four-year term; the 30-day statutory deadline to fill it (N.J.S.A. 40A:16-1 et seq.) was reported as Oct 12, which dates the resignation to Sept 12 2025. William 'Bill' Harrison, 38-year chair of the township Zoning Board, was appointed and sworn in Tuesday Oct 7 2025 (weekday checks out) by unanimous vote. Seat vacant 2025-09-12 to 2025-10-07. No mid-term change found in any ward seat, and no change to the mayoralty between elections, in any panel year.

Sources that failed. (a) montclairnjusa.org (township site) returns HTTP 403 to BOTH curl-with-browser-UA and WebFetch, on the council page and the clerk's Elections page - no route in found. (b) ecode360.com/MO0769/documents/Minutes, the archive the census recorded, is behind a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' interstitial: 403 to curl on the HTML listing, on /Minutes.json, and on /api/documents?customerId=MO0769. There is no reachable eCode360 JSON endpoint; treat the census's Montclair archive entry as DEAD to non-browser tools. (c) baristanet.com now 301-redirects and its content has been folded into montclairlocal.news (Montclair Local republishes 'Baristanet Profile' pieces), so Baristanet is not a separate source. (d) essexclerk.com serves no robots.txt (404) and served everything to curl.

MAYOR SELECTION: directly elected, not council-selected. Proof is structural rather than charter-quoted - 'Mayor-Montclair' / 'For Mayor for Montclair' is a contest on the county clerk's official canvass in both 2020 and 2024, with named candidates and vote totals. Montclair's council-manager form (1923 Municipal Manager Act) puts executive authority in an appointed Township Manager while the mayor is popularly elected as a member of the council; the day-to-day municipal executive in the panel window was Township Manager Timothy Stafford, then interim/permanent manager Stephen D. Marks. Cross-confirmed by the NJ DCA Mayors Directory JSON API (data.nj.gov/resource/gkt3-i954.json?$q=Montclair), which returns muni_name 'Montclair Township', county Essex, mayor Renee Baskerville, term_start 2024-07-01. NOTE the DCA record's term_end of 2026-12-31 is WRONG - Montclair terms run to 2028-06-30; do not trust DCA term_end. PRESIDING OFFICER: 'The council shall appoint a deputy mayor from its membership to serve a term to be determined by the council' (township code, quoted verbatim in montclairlocal.news/2019/08/deputy-mayor-montclair-nj/). No fixed term, hence the rotation disputes. RUNOFFS: none required or held. 2020 mayor was decided at 50.66%; the 2024 3rd Ward was won on a 45% plurality (Williams 624 of 1390 cast) with no June runoff, confirming NJ nonpartisan May elections in Montclair are decided by plurality. NO seat count change across the panel: 7 elected seats in every year 2019-2026.

CAVEATS on individual rows, filed here rather than as gaps because each seat-year involved is sourced. (1) Deputy Mayor, 2019-01-01 to 2019-06-25: recorded to Sean Spiller at LOW confidence. The August 2019 article establishes the 2016 slate's agreed rotation (1st Ward Hurlock, then 2nd Ward Schlager, then 3rd Ward Spiller, then 4th Ward Baskerville) and states that 'Hurlock, Schlager and Spiller have finished their terms as deputy mayor' as of the June 25 2019 vote - so Spiller was the immediately preceding holder. His actual start date predates the panel window and is unknown; 2019-01-01 is a window-clip, not a sourced date. (2) Deputy Mayor, 2020-07-01 to 2024-06-30: recorded to William Hurlock at LOW confidence. He is named 'Deputy Mayor Bill Hurlock' in October 2023 and 'former Deputy Mayor William Hurlock' in a May 2025 correction notice, but no source was found fixing the start of his deputy-mayor term or ruling out a rotation within that council; 2020-07-01 is the term boundary, inferred. (3) Deputy Mayor, Susan Shin Andersen from 2024-07-01: MEDIUM. She is repeatedly titled Deputy Mayor from September 2025 through May 2026; the 2024-07-01 start is inferred from the term boundary. (4) AT-LARGE SEAT LABELS ARE AN ANALYTIC CONVENTION. Montclair's two at-large seats are elected on one Vote-For-2 line and are not numbered on the ballot, so no seat identity exists in the source record. 'At-Large A' and 'At-Large B' were assigned so that each documented succession chain stays inside one label: A = Russo (2016-2024) then Andersen; B = McMahon then Yacobellis -> Terry (documented replacement) then Loughman -> Harrison (documented replacement). Only the two appointment chains are evidentiary; the pairing across the 2020 and 2024 elections is arbitrary.

FUTURE CYCLE IN WINDOW, deliberately NOT written as a cycle row. Because Loughman resigned after the Aug 21 2025 ballot deadline, her unexpired at-large term goes before the voters at the November 2026 general election; Harrison holds the seat by appointment until then, and the winner serves to 2028-07-01. Petitions became available 2026-07-10 with an Aug 20 2026 filing deadline. As of 2026-08-17 that election has not occurred, so recording it as a cycle would create a spurious 'flagged' row; Harrison's tenure is carried as ongoing through 2026. Re-run this city after November 2026.
8 seats (Mayor, Deputy Mayor, At-Large A, At-Large B, Ward 1-4) x 8 years = 64 seat-years, all covered by tenures. 0 gaps. 27 tenure rows.
